# What Changed in Dimorphos’s Orbit After DART

Before the impact, Dimorphos took 11 hours and 55 minutes to orbit the larger asteroid Didymos. Immediately afterward, its orbital period was 11 hours, 22 minutes and 37 seconds—a shortening of 32 minutes and 42 seconds.

Over the following weeks, Dimorphos lost more rocky material to space as its orbital period continued to shorten. The period eventually settled at 11 hours, 22 minutes and 3 seconds, which the Narrative describes as 33 minutes and 15 seconds shorter than before impact. The orbit was also no longer circular after the impact.
